summary: WP-009 reviewed: #/notes route registration, Notes nav link in index.html, nav-highlight active-state logic, and the full notes-collected.js view. All four acceptance criteria are met. No blocking issues found.
nav-highlight.js: Correct prefix-match logic with '#/' exclusion guard. Clean, minimal, well-documented. initNavHighlight() called once at app boot (not per navigation) — no listener leak.

notes-collected.js: Excellent code quality. XSS safety enforced via textContent throughout and encodeURIComponent in URL construction. Accessibility well-handled (aria-live='polite', <details>/<summary>, <button type='button'>). Debounced auto-save with status feedback is clean. The forward-declare sidebar pattern is correctly explained with an inline comment.

Stale-timer edge case noted (user navigates away with debounce pending): the timer fires a valid API save on detached DOM — expected auto-save behavior, not a bug. Status element operations on detached DOM are no-ops. No memory leak.
app.js route registration is well-organized. WP numbers in inline comments are cross-plan historical references — consistent with existing codebase convention.

comments.note: notes-collected.js — handleSave only adds '.has-notes' when notes is truthy (correct); removal is delegated to handleCardEmpty. The split responsibility is correct and safe, but worth a short inline comment on handleSave noting 'removal handled by handleCardEmpty on empty save' to aid future contributors.

[documentation-forward] notes-collected.js module docstring is thorough on layout and UX behavior, but does not mention the normaliseNotesResponse normalisation step or the in-memory notesMap pattern. A brief mention would help contributors understand the data flow without reading the full function body.
No blocking or architectural issues found. Code is clean, consistent with project idioms, and all four AC are fully met.

summary: Addressed Reviewer documentation-forward: added a 'Data flow' section to the notes-collected.js module docstring describing (1) the api.notes.list() fetch, (2) normaliseNotesResponse() PascalCase→camelCase normalization, and (3) the notesMap in-memory Map pattern that keeps sidebar indicators and new cards in sync with saves.

Project manifest docs (api-surface.md, gui-frontend.md) were already current: api-surface.md documents both renderNotesCollected (with normaliseNotesResponse reference) and normaliseNotesResponse itself; gui-frontend.md has a thorough #/notes route entry. No changes needed there.
All four acceptance criteria confirmed met by prior implementation and QA pipelines.
